## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Suttaviññatti* ("Asking for thread"), cataloged as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 26, is a disciplinary rule from the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating monastic robe production [SuttaCentral]. According to the rule, a Buddhist monk who solicits or asks for thread and subsequently has robe-cloth woven from it incurs an offense requiring forfeiture of the cloth (*nissaggiya*) and confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations of the text into English include that of Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this training rule is widely attested across early Buddhist monastic lineages [SuttaCentral]. In the Pali tradition, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Nissaggiya Pācittiya 26 and Bhikkhu Parivāra Nissaggiya Pācittiya 26, alongside a counterpart in the nuns' discipline (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Nissaggiya Pācittiya 27) [SuttaCentral]. Beyond the Theravāda tradition, parallel Vinaya rules and Prātimokṣa entries are preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions across several schools, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda traditions [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus indicates extensive formulaic sharing within the Pali canon, recording 498 matching passages across 112 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal overlaps occur with other disciplinary analyses in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, notably Nissaggiya Pācittiya rules 12, 21, 7, and 19, as well as the *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* (Kd 15) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus match segments of the rule with Tibetan translations of canonical and commentarial Vinaya literature, such as the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3), the *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005), and Vinaya commentaries like the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104) [DharmaNexus].
